newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain-based Intoil lifts 1996 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain-based Intoil lifts 1996 net profit.

text.p: Intoil E.C., a Bahrain-based oil and gas company, said on Sunday it posted a record $4 million in net profit in 1996, up 21 percent from $3.3 million in 1995.
Its Chairman, Hassan Fakhro, attributed the increase in profit to higher prices during 1996 and an improvement in oil and gas reserves.
Fakhro said in a statement that a barrel of West Texas Intermediate averaged $22.20 in 1996 compared with $18.42 in 1995 and $17.19 in 1994.

"It is very apparent that oil prices have entered an era of firmness in comparison to the last decade. Although we may see some weaknesses in the immediate future, it is likely that prices will be reasonably firm and stable," Fakhro said.
Established in 1984, Intoil operates in the international energy industry, primarily in the U.S. oil and gas sector.

The firm, through its wholly owned U.S. subsidiary, Intoil Inc, headquartered in Colorado, owns and operates oil and gas reserves in more than 12 states with major interests in the Rocky Mountain region, Texas and Oklahoma.
